title: Streaming boundary probe and KV-prefix guard for graceful structured-output resumption
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We frequently observe partial structured JSON outputs from the streaming API when connections are interrupted or when downstream proxies truncate responses. This causes broken tool/function calls and client-side parsing errors. The current retry strategies either replay whole prompts (costly) or attempt naive string stitching (brittle). Goal: implement a low-cost, reliable server-side resumption mechanism that preserves tool-call boundaries, avoids duplicating expensive model prefixes, and provides a clear client guidance for retries.
proposed_solution: Introduce a three-part protocol: (1) stream-boundary probe token(s) emitted periodically to mark safe resumption points, (2) a KV-prefix guard that ensures resumed generation includes a minimal verified context suffix rather than the entire prompt, and (3) idempotent resume handshake with an explicit 'resume_token' and last-acknowledged-byte index. The runtime will emit sentinel probes only when structured output is enabled for a route to avoid spamming raw text users.
design_notes:
- Probe format is an NDJSON control line: {"_probe":"v1","pos":12345}
 to avoid colliding with tool payloads.
- KV-prefix guard: on resume request, client supplies resume_token + short context hash; server reconstructs minimal KV-cached state to warm placement.
- Backfill policy: server attempts partial object repair using deterministic heuristics (e.g., close last open JSON brace, re-run lightweight sanitizer) but will prefer canonical resume over lossy auto-repair for tool calls.
- Streaming compatibility layer: fall back to existing resumable semantics for clients not opting into structured probes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Client can request resume with resume_token and receive a deterministic continuation without duplicating model-costly prefix in 95% of observed truncated cases.
2) Tool/function call boundaries are preserved; downstream tool invocation payloads are either complete or a precise resume point is signaled for caller retry.
3) No regressions in latency p95 for routes without structured probes (<= 5% change).
4) Automated fuzz tests covering truncated UTF-8, nested JSON, and interleaved toolcall markers pass in CI.
5) Conformance tests for clients that do and do not support probes succeed against a compatibility shim.
6) Documentation and SDK changes shipped with examples for ephemeral resume tokens and best-practice retry backoffs.
7) Security review completed and KMS integration checks for tokens passed.
8) Monitoring: dashboard shows resumed_count, successful_resume_rate, and any increased duplicate-toolcall incidents.
milestones: Integration with KV cache warmup + e2e tests (2026-03-19)
Canary rollout on 10% of structured routes (2026-03-22)
testing_plan: Unit: probe encoder/decoder, resume_token integrity, context-hash verification
Integration: simulate abrupt connection close at multiple byte offsets with and without toolcall payloads
Fuzz: interleave UTF-8 boundaries, escape sequences, and large nested objects
Load: check p95 latency on non-probe routes to validate negligible overhead
Chaos: terminate KV-cache restore mid-resume and verify safe fallback to canary policy
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated on route boolean structured_resume_enabled
Internal SDKs enabled by default in canary to instrument client guidance
Gradual traffic ramp (0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback on duplicate-toolcall spike
Alerting: resume_failure_rate > 3% for 5m triggers immediate rollback
risks: Probe token could be accidentally treated as user payload by naive parsers — mitigated by conservative probe schema and SDK parsers
KV warmup may add tail latency for first resume path — mitigated by short context hashes and pre-warmed hot keys
Duplicate tool invocation if client and server both retry — mitigated by idempotency tokens and server-side duplicate detection
Attack surface: resume_token theft could be used to infer partial outputs — mitigated by one-time tokens and KMS signing
open_questions: What is the recommended TTL for resume_token? (30s vs 5m vs session-scoped)
Should probes be emitted for all structured outputs or only for routes with explicit tool calling enabled?
How to represent probe metadata in streaming wire formats besides NDJSON (e.g., SSE, chunked HTTP)?
Do we allow client-supplied heuristics to opt-in for aggressive auto-repair of truncated JSON?
